kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-08.title: Mower-hours
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-08.body:
Two mowers for 10 hours is $2 \times 10 = 20$ mower-hours of work. Five mowers share these 20 mower-hours: $20 \div 5 = 4$ hours.

**Answer: (D) 4 hours**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-08.title: One mower first
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-08.body:
One mower alone would need twice as long as two mowers: 20 hours. Five mowers need a fifth of that: 4 hours.

**Answer: (D) 4 hours**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-09.title: Compare the times for one turn
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-09.body:
The second hand goes round once in 1 minute. The hour hand goes round once in 12 hours $= 12 \times 60 = 720$ minutes. So the second hand is $720$ times faster.

**Answer: (E) 720 times**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-09.title: Via the minute hand
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-09.body:
The second hand is 60 times faster than the minute hand (1 minute vs 60 minutes per turn), and the minute hand is 12 times faster than the hour hand (1 hour vs 12 hours). Together $60 \times 12 = 720$.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-16.title: Ann first, then Bill
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-16.body:
Think of the 6 marbles as different objects. Ann can take any of the 6 marbles. For Bill to win, he must take one of the 2 remaining marbles of the same colour. That is $6 \times 2 = 12$ ways.

**Answer: (E) 12**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-16.title: By colour
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-16.body:
Both red: Ann takes one of 3 reds, Bill one of the 2 other reds: $3 \times 2 = 6$ ways. Both blue: also 6 ways. Total 12.

**Answer: (E) 12**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-17.title: Pretend there are 10 students
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-17.body:
The answer does not depend on the class size, so imagine 10 students. Together they scored $10 \times 6 = 60$ points. The 6 who passed scored $6 \times 8 = 48$. The 4 who failed scored $60 - 48 = 12$, i.e. $12 \div 4 = 3$ on average.

**Answer: (C) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-17.title: Weighted mean
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-17.body:
Let $m$ be the mean of those who failed. Then $0.6 \cdot 8 + 0.4 \cdot m = 6$, so $0.4m = 1.2$ and $m = 3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-19.title: Use the area formula
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-19.body:
Let the height be $h$; then the side is $\frac{3}{5}h$. Area $= \frac12 \cdot \frac35 h \cdot h = \frac{3}{10}h^2 = 120$, so $h^2 = 400$ and $h = 20$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 20**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-19.title: Parts
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-19.body:
Write side $= 3t$, height $= 5t$. Area $= \frac12 \cdot 3t \cdot 5t = 7.5t^2 = 120$, so $t^2 = 16$, $t = 4$, height $= 20$ cm (side 12 cm; check $\frac12 \cdot 12 \cdot 20 = 120$).

**Answer: (A) 20**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-20.title: Equations
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-20.body:
Let Albert have $a$ and Ben $b$ marbles. First condition: $a - 6 = b + 6$, so $a = b + 12$.

Second: after giving half away Albert has $\frac a2$ and Ben has $b + \frac a2$, so $b + \frac a2 = \frac a2 + 8$, i.e. $b = 8$. Then $a = 20$ and the total is $28$.

**Answer: (D) 28**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-20.title: Think it through
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-20.body:
When Albert gives half of his marbles away, both boys get the same "half of Albert", so the 8 extra marbles of Ben are exactly what Ben had at the start: $b = 8$. Giving 6 marbles evens them out, so Albert has 12 more than Ben: 20. Total $20 + 8 = 28$.

**Answer: (D) 28**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-24.title: Subtract the outside triangles
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-24.body:
Let $AD = a$, $BC = 3a$ and the height be $h$. Area of $ABCD = \frac{a + 3a}{2} h = 2ah = 32$, so $ah = 16$.

Triangle $AMN$ is the trapezoid minus three triangles:
- $ABM$: base $BM = \frac{3a}{2}$, height $h$: area $\frac34 ah = 12$.
- $MCN$: $N$ is the midpoint of $CD$, so it lies halfway between the parallel lines $AD$ and $BC$: its height above $BC$ is $\frac h2$; base $MC = \frac{3a}{2}$: area $\frac12 \cdot \frac{3a}{2}\cdot\frac h2 = \frac38 ah = 6$.
- $ADN$: base $AD = a$, and $N$ is $\frac h2$ below $AD$: area $\frac12 \cdot a \cdot \frac h2 = \frac14 ah = 4$.

Area $AMN = 32 - 12 - 6 - 4 = 10$.

**Answer: (B) 10**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-25.title: Write the totals
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-25.body:
If on day 1 Tom caught $t$, Bob $b$ and Rob $r$ mice, the totals are
- Tom: $t + 2t + 4t = 7t$,
- Bob: $b + (b+2) + (b+4) = 3b + 6$,
- Rob: $3r$.

All are equal, so $7t$ is a multiple of 3, hence $t$ is a multiple of 3. $t = 0$ would give $3b + 6 = 0$, impossible. So the smallest is $t = 3$: total 21, $b = 5$, $r = 7$.

On the first day they caught $3 + 5 + 7 = 15$ mice. Larger $t$ ($6, 9, \dots$) gives more mice on every day.

**Answer: (B) 15**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-26.title: Primes adding to 50
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-26.body:
The two side lengths add up to half the perimeter: $p + q = 50$. If one of them were 2, the other would be 48, not prime. So both are odd primes. List $p \le q$:
- $3 + 47$, $7 + 43$, $13 + 37$, $19 + 31$.
(5 + 45, 11 + 39, 17 + 33, 23 + 27 fail; 25 + 25 is not prime.)

These 4 rectangles have different areas ($141, 301, 481, 589$).

**Answer: (A) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-30.title: Look at the quotient
kangaroo-ca-2015-g0708-30.body:
A remainder is smaller than the divisor, so for divisors $n \le 600$ the remainder is at most 599.

- $601 \le n \le 671$: $3n \le 2013 < 2015 < 4n$, so the remainder is $2015 - 3n \le 2015 - 1803 = 212$. Too small.
- $672 \le n \le 1000$: $2n \le 2015 < 3n$, so the remainder is $2015 - 2n$. It is greater than 600 when $2n < 1415$, i.e. $n \le 707$.

So the divisors $672, 673, \dots, 707$ work: $707 - 672 + 1 = 36$ of them.

**Answer: (D) 36**
